title.narrative: Operating the dialysis center at Banadir Hospital in Mogadishu

description.narrative: Providing health care services represented by providing the necessary treatment in the city of Mogadishu to preserve the lives of patients with kidney disease and renal failure resulting from the lack of treatment and thus reducing the number of deaths by providing free treatment.

Providing the need to cover the treatment of patients with renal failure and ensuring that they receive the necessary treatment free of charge, with an expected number of 10,800 dialysis sessions and 2,760 medical services in the kidney disease clinic, supporting the steadfastness of the medical and technical staff and reducing the migration of (50) medical and technical staff with the localization of the service.

The project is to operate an integrated center for treating patients with renal failure through hemodialysis in the state of Banadir in the city of Mogadishu. It is considered the only free specialized center of its kind in the region and is directly responsible for providing service to patients with renal failure and kidney disease. The project, at the current stage, aims to provide its services to 330 patients. One person per month, including 100 dialysis patients registered in the records of the dialysis center and receiving services ranging between two and three dialysis sessions per week, meaning 850 regular sessions and an average of 50 emergency sessions per month, meaning about 900 dialysis sessions per month, thus covering 10,800 sessions for patients. The entire duration of the project is 12 months, as the center was built in 2017 by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and has been equipped since that year with 25 devices, currently 20 of which are operable, in addition to a water treatment plant to feed these devices. The center is located within the main hospital in Banadir, where it is possible The center has a capacity of approximately 35 daily sessions, equivalent to 900 sessions per month, in addition to the presence of a pharmacy that provides special medicines for patients with kidney failure. The center also includes a clinic specializing in kidney diseases, which is considered the only one that provides its services for free in Mogadishu. The need to support the project comes due to the absence of specialized centers. In this area in Mogadishu, due to the health sector being damaged by conflict during the conflict period in recent years, in addition to the weak capabilities of most private health facilities or the low level of services, the high financial cost of treatment and the inability of many patients to bear the costs of treatment, according to a multiple needs assessment. Sectors From the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), a wide segment of the population has faced problems accessing life-saving health services, with an estimated 71 percent of the population living below the poverty line amid chronic crises while Somalia also continues to show some of the highest mortality rates. While the coronavirus has exacerbated these dynamics, with up to 20 percent of Somalia's population (3.5 million people) expected to suffer from the direct and indirect effects of the pandemic.
